hypothesis_name: Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (PEAD) in Indian Equities
economic_rationale: Quarterly earnings surprises create persistent price momentum as institutional investors gradually re-allocate capital following analyst earnings estimate revisions. Under-reaction to fundamental disclosures allows post-announcement price drift.
behavioural_rationale: Investors exhibit anchoring bias to pre-earnings valuation models and conservatism bias when processing new financial disclosures, causing delayed price adjustment.
expected_market_behaviour: Outperformance of stocks exhibiting strong positive earnings surprise over 10-60 session holding horizon.
falsification_criteria: Expectancy R < 0.25R or Profit Factor < 1.30 on DEVELOPMENT dataset under FORCE_CLOSE policy.
supporting_literature: Bernard & Thomas (1989) - Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift: Delayed Price Response or Risk Premium?
Ball & Brown (1968) - An Empirical Evaluation of Accounting Income Numbers
Rendleman, Jones, & Latané (1982) - Empirical Anomaly or Inefficient Markets?
